prompt: Create one photographic editorial still-life image for a software portfolio project called Doxxme, a satirical hackathon app about trading your digital privacy for money. No words, no logos, no interface, no lettering, no screenshot, no fake device, no illustration, no Polaroid border. Landscape 4:3 composition suitable for a small printed photograph. Real-camera aesthetic, close candid tabletop photography with subtle film grain and actual material imperfections. Subject: a plain pale-yellow paper envelope lying open on a dark walnut desk. A small unbranded brass padlock lies unlocked on the envelope, its open shackle clearly visible, with exactly three ordinary unmarked metal coins nearby. Understated visual joke about selling privacy. Strong simple silhouettes readable at thumbnail size. Soft afternoon side light, warm yellow and tobacco brown, natural contact shadows, moderate depth of field. Objects look commonplace and used, not glossy designer products. No readable coin inscriptions, no identifying personal documents, no hackers, no eyes, no neon, no floating graphics, no symmetrical flat lay. This is conceptual cover art rather than documentation of a physical product.
